October gives you plenty of reasons to post something other than property. Some are an opportunity to show a little personality, while others give you a reason to talk about your community or the way you work.

You don't need to use them all. Pick the ones that feel relevant to you and your audience, then use the ideas below as a starting point.

All month · Stoptober

What are you giving up?

Stoptober might officially be about quitting smoking, but social media has given the idea a life of its own. Your take on it doesn't need to be serious. It's a chance to show some personality and the everyday reality of life as an estate agent.

Share something you're genuinely trying to cut back on this month, or have fun with what you'd like to give up. Last-minute viewing cancellations. Chasing solicitors. Checking Rightmove when you're technically off the clock. The more recognisable it is, the more people will engage with it.

Try: a short team video where everyone names the one thing they'd quit if they could.

10 October · World Mental Health Day

A little understanding can go a long way.

Moving home can be stressful. There's uncertainty, pressure, a lot of waiting and plenty that's outside your client's control. World Mental Health Day is a good moment to think about the small things you do to make that feel a little easier.

Think clear communication, explaining what happens next, or simply being available when someone needs an answer. None of it is complicated, but it's what clients remember. Good service often comes down to remembering there's a person behind every move.

Try: a simple post sharing one thing your team always does to keep buyers and sellers in the loop.

16 October · World Food Day

Use your local platform for something that matters.

World Food Day raises awareness of hunger and food insecurity around the world. You can bring it much closer to home by highlighting the people and organisations helping in your own community.

Share a local food bank, community kitchen or collection point, along with what they currently need. Or simply encourage your audience to support them if they can. You've built an audience that cares about your area, and this is a genuine way to put it to use.

Try: set up a collection point in your office and share a photo of the donations as they build up.

25 October · Clocks go back

An extra hour. What are you doing with yours?

The clocks going back doesn't need a complicated property angle. It's something everyone relates to, which makes it an easy opportunity for a simple, personality-led post.

Ask your audience what they're doing with their extra hour, or share your own. A lie-in, a Sunday walk, breakfast somewhere local, or, let's be honest, checking Rightmove.

Try: a poll on your Stories with three or four options, then share the results the following day.

31 October · Halloween

Give people a reason to get out locally.

Halloween is a great excuse to create genuinely useful local content, especially for families looking for something to do over half-term or on the night itself.

Round up nearby pumpkin patches, Halloween trails, best-decorated streets or family events. Better still, ask your followers for their recommendations and build the list from the comments. It's helpful, it's shareable, and it shows people you actually know the area.

Try: post your roundup a week early so families have time to plan, then reshare it on the day.

You don't need to use every date on this list. In fact, we'd rather you didn't.

Pick the ones that actually fit you, your business and your local audience. A couple of relevant posts that feel genuinely yours will always be more useful than filling your calendar for the sake of it.

And if October has made one thing easier, you've already got five fewer days staring at a blank content calendar.
